method: scripts/ib-research/claim-check.js: the passage is copied verbatim from the live source text at the pinned revision; VERIFIED = every claim number in one sentence that shares >= 50% of the claim's content words

records.claim: It was the first object identified in the asteroid belt, discovered on 1 January 1801 by Giuseppe Piazzi at Palermo Astronomical Observatory, and announced as a new planet.
records.passage: It was the first object identified in the asteroid belt, discovered on 1 January 1801 by Giuseppe Piazzi at Palermo Astronomical Observatory in Sicily, and announced as a new planet.

records.claim: Ceres's diameter was determined to within ten percent of its true value of 939 km (583 mi).
records.passage: In the 1970s, infrared photometry enabled more accurate measurements of its albedo, and Ceres's diameter was determined to within ten percent of its true value of 939 km (583 mi).

records.claim: Herschel underestimated its diameter at 260 km in 1802; in 1811, Schröter overestimated it at 2,613 km.
records.passage: Herschel underestimated its diameter at 260 km (160 mi) in 1802; in 1811, German astronomer Johann Hieronymus Schröter overestimated it at 2,613 km (1,624 mi).

records.claim: A formula predicted another planet with an orbital radius near 2.8 astronomical units (AU), or 420 million km, from the Sun.
records.passage: This formula predicted that there ought to be another planet with an orbital radius near 2.8 astronomical units (AU), or 420 million km, from the Sun.

narration.text: Why Ceres was called a planet in 1801.
Giuseppe Piazzi spotted it between Mars and Jupiter.
It sits about 420 million kilometres from the Sun.
Early estimates ranged from 260 to 2,613 kilometres wide.
As more belt objects appeared, it lost planet status.
So the asteroid belt's giant was a planet for a while.
